Several AI agents powered by Grok Bot work together as one algorithm:

1. CCI detects when BTC moves unusually far from its recent average

The bot calculates the typical BTC level for each candle:

Typical = (High + Low + Close) / 3
CCI = (Typical - SMA) / (0.015 × Mean Deviation)

Where Mean Deviation measures the average absolute distance from the SMA

Then:
CCI below -100 → unusually weak movement
CCI above +100 → unusually strong movement

An extreme reading creates a possible reversal setup, but the bot does not immediately act on it

2. Double EMA confirms whether BTC has started moving away from that extreme
The system calculates:

DEMA = 2 × EMA - EMA(EMA)

Unlike a traditional EMA, Double EMA reduces lag and responds faster to changes in direction

Then:
CCI recovering above -100 + DEMA rising → stronger Up signal
CCI falling below +100 + DEMA declining → stronger Down signal

The bot waits for both the extreme reading and the directional reversal to align

Here’s how the algorithm works:

> PULSE identifies the side with stronger demand

I = (D_in - D_out) / (D_in + D_out)

Compares the queues for entering and exiting longs at the top of each Up and Down book. Identifies stronger demand on the entry side and passes the book state to IMPACT. Skips empty books

> IMPACT estimates the potential quote move

v = b + α + βI

Uses historical observations to link the imbalance to subsequent changes in the available exit level. Works over a short horizon that ends before the market expires

Passes EDGE an estimate of the level at which the long could be closed

> EDGE checks whether an edge remains

e = v - a - c

Compares the estimated exit level with the available entry level and total round-trip costs. Selects the side with the greater positive edge between Up and Down

If the edge does not cover an additional buffer, the trade is skipped

> SIZE limits position size

Q = min(B/L, D, Q_cap)

Sizes the position using a risk budget and a stressed adverse move. Then caps it by order book depth, available collateral, and total exposure, including open orders

> ENTRY executes the allocated size

ℓ_max = v - c - ε

Sends an order with a maximum entry level. The available portion fills, and the remainder is canceled

Checks the tick size and valid range. Passes only confirmed fills to EXIT

> EXIT completes the trade

PnL = Q_fill × (b_exit - ℓ_fill) - C

Closes the position when order book pressure reverses, a risk stop triggers, or the chosen holding horizon ends

Uses average execution levels and includes all costs. Feeds the result back to IMPACT to check model quality

Here’s how the algorithm works:

> MONITOR gathers the context for entry

x = (Return, Gap, Volatility, Spread)

Tracks the underlying asset’s movement, its position relative to the reference level, and CLOB data. Adds the time remaining and order book depth

Passes the collected data on both sides of the market, Up and Down, to INFER

> INFER assesses three types of movement

pₖ = πₖLₖ / ΣⱼπⱼLⱼ

Applies Gaussian Naive Bayes to rising, falling, and range-bound quote movements over the selected horizon

Trains on completed observations from comparable assets and market windows. Uses Gaussian feature distributions for upward, downward, and sideways conditions

> EXPECT checks whether the trade makes sense

e = Σₖpₖgₖ - c

Combines the scenario estimates with their average results in comparable historical entries. Subtracts round-trip costs

Only passes on a positive edge with a buffer, calculated for the selected size and horizon

> DOUBT filters out ambiguous conditions

H = -Σₖpₖln(pₖ)

Checks how the estimate is distributed across the three scenarios. Skips a new entry when the distribution is too uniform

Tunes the threshold on held-out historical data. Compares the estimates with observed movement frequencies

> RESERVE limits total exposure

Q_free = max(0, Q_limit-Q_held-Q_pending)

Calculates the remaining limit after accounting for the position and unfilled entries. Caps the new size by available collateral and CLOB depth

If the final size changes, EXPECT recalculates the costs

> ROUTER synchronizes entry and exit

t_exit = t_signal + h

Submits a limit entry order, checks fills, and initiates the exit at the time for which INFER estimated the movement

Accounts for partial fills and feeds completed results back to INFER. All exits are scheduled before the market window ends

Several AI agents powered by Grok Bot work together as one algorithm:

1. Kalman Filter separates BTC's underlying movement from short-term noise

Instead of following every BTC tick, the bot continuously updates a smoother estimate:

Estimateₜ = Estimateₜ₋₁ + Kₜ × (BTCₜ − Estimateₜ₋₁)

Kₜ controls how much weight the algorithm gives each new observation

The result follows meaningful BTC movement while reducing the influence of temporary fluctuations

2. Standardized Deviation identifies when BTC moves unusually far from that estimate

The system measures the difference relative to recent noise:
Z = (BTC − Estimate) / σ

A reading above +2 means BTC is unusually far above its estimated level. Below -2 means the opposite

The bot looks for a return toward the estimate before entering a reversal trade:

Above +2 and turning lower → Down setup
Below -2 and turning higher → Up setup
